questions.question: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 aims to provide ____ days of wage employment to every household to ensure livelihood security in rural areas.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__100.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) aims to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.**
 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MNREGA) is **an Indian labour law and social security measure that aims to guarantee the right to work.**
 
• The act was passed on** August 23, 2005. (under the prime ministership of Manmohan Singh).**
 
• The act was** first proposed in 1991 by PV.Narasimha Rao.**
 
• It was quoted as a **"Stellar Example of Rural Development" in World Development Report 2014.**
 
• The NDA Government had decided to provide 150 days in rain-hit areas.
 
• Employment is provided within 5 km of an applicant's residence.
 
• If work is not provided within 15 days of applying, applicants are entitled to an unemployment allowance.
 
• The registration process involves an application to the Gram Panchayat and the issue of Job cards.
 
• **MNREGA is implemented mainly by Gram Panchayats.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The act aims to follow** Directive Principles of State Policy enunciated in Part 4** of the Constitution of India.
 
• **Article 41** directs the state to secure all the citizens'** right to Work.**
 
• The act also fulfills** Article 21 **of the Constitution of India which guarantees the** Right to Life with dignity to every citizen of India.**

questions.question: Which of the following was set up in 1956 by the Indian government by nationalising all the existing private sector life insurance companies?

The correct answer is __**Life Insurance Corporation of India**__

__
 
• **Life Insurance Company is a public sector insurance company headquartered in Mumbai that was incorporated by Insurance Act in June 1956.**
 
• It was established on 1st September 1956 and currently, it has 8 zonal offices and over 2000 branch offices.
 
• **In 1956, the government nationalized over 200 private Indian and foreign insurance providers under a roof named LIC. Hence option 3 is correct.**
 
• In 1818, Oriental Life Insurance Company located in Calcutta was the first insurance company in India which was established by Europeans.

• **The New India Insurance Company of India Limited is India's largest public sector general insurance company headquartered in Mumbai.**

questions.question: Which of the following sectors had the largest percentage of workforce in urban India in the year 2019-2020?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Service**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The service sector dominated the urban workforce in India in 2019-2020.
 
• Approximately 60% of the urban workforce was employed in the service sector during this period.
 
• The service sector includes industries like IT, retail, hospitality, healthcare, and education.
 
• This sector's growth is attributed to the rapid urbanization and increased demand for professional services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urbanization in India**

 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increasing population in urban areas compared to rural areas.
 
• India has seen a steady increase in urbanization, with urban population growing from 27.81% in 2001 to 34.93% in 2020.
 
• Economic opportunities, better living standards, and improved infrastructure are key drivers of urbanization.
 
 
 
• **Growth of the IT Sector**
 
 
• The IT sector has been a significant contributor to the service industry in urban India.
 
• India is a global leader in IT services, outsourcing, and software development.
 
• This sector provides employment to millions of professionals in urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Employment Distribution**
 
 
• Employment in urban areas is mainly concentrated in the service sector, followed by industry and agriculture.
 
• Industries such as manufacturing, construction, and mining also play a role, but to a lesser extent.
 
 
 
• **Economic Contribution**
 
 
• The service sector is the largest contributor to India's GDP, accounting for around 54% as of 2020.
 
• This sector's significant contribution highlights its importance in the overall economic landscape of the country.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a private sector industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tata Iron and Steel Company**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO)**, now known as Tata Steel, is a private sector company in India.
 
• Founded in **1907 by Jamsetji Tata**, Tata Steel is one of the world's largest private steel manufacturers.
 
• Tata Steel operates independently of government control and is part of the **Tata Group**, a private conglomerate.
 
• It is headquartered in Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, and has operations across multiple countries.
 
• Unlike public sector companies like the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Tata Steel is listed as a private enterprise, representing India's thriving private industrial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Public Sector Enterprises**

 
 
• These are companies where the majority stake (51% or more) is owned by the government.
 
• Examples include Life Insurance Corporation (LIC), Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL), and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).
 
• They are primarily established to serve public interests and contribute to national development.
 
 
 
• **Private Sector Enterprises**
 
 
• These are owned, managed, and controlled by private individuals or corporations.
 
• Examples include Tata Steel, Reliance Industries, Infosys, and Wipro.
 
• Private companies focus on profit generation and operate in a competitive market environment.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Public and Private Sector**
 
 
• Ownership: Public sector is government-owned, while private sector is privately owned.
 
• Objective: Public sector focuses on welfare and development, while private sector aims at profitability.
 
• Examples: Public sector includes entities like ONGC, while private sector includes companies like Tata Group.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the Private Sector in India**
 
 
• Drives economic growth through innovation and competitiveness.
 
• Provides employment opportunities to a large section of the population.
 
• Plays a key role in the globalization of Indian industries, contributing to exports and foreign investments.

questions.question: Hindustan Aeronautics limited comes under which sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Public sector**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) **is an Indian state-owned **aerospace and defence company headquartered in Bangalore, India.**
 
• It is governed under the **management of the Indian Ministry of Defence.**
 
• The **public sector consists of organizations and institutions owned and operated by the government.**
 
• They provide services to the public, and the revenue comes from the government treasury.
 
• **HAL **is involved in the **operations of the aerospace industry, including the manufacturing and assembly of aircraft, navigation, and related communication equipment, as well as operating airports.**
 
• It provides these services to the **Indian Armed Forces predominantly and has a significant role in the defense sector of the country.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Sector
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Co-operative Sector
 
 
 
• This sector includes organizations run by the people themselves for mutual benefit.
 
• They aren't owned by the state and their aim is to serve the interests of their members rather than to earn profits.
 
• Examples include credit unions, cooperative housing, and farmers' co-ops.
 
 
 
 

 Private Sector
 
 
 
• The private sector consists of organizations and institutions that are not controlled by the government.
 
• These organizations are run by individuals or companies with the aim of making a profit.
 
• Examples include private companies like Tata Motors, Reliance Industries, and Infosys.
 
 
 
 

 Foreign Sector

• These can include multinational corporations, international organizations, and foreign governments.
 
• Examples would be companies like Microsoft, Toyota, and Nestle operating in India.

questions.question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?

options.text: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building
Social mobilisation, economic development, and education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Social mobilisation** refers to the process of bringing together all societal sectors to raise awareness, demand, and participation for the empowerment and development of Self-Help Groups (SHGs).
 
• **Capital formation** involves the accumulation of assets and investments to generate income and enhance the financial stability of SHGs.
 
• **Capacity building** focuses on enhancing the skills, knowledge, and abilities of SHG members to improve their organizational and operational efficiency.
 
• These three components together aim to strengthen SHGs, enabling them to become self-reliant and sustainable in their economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**:

 
 
• SHGs are small, economically homogeneous affinity groups of rural poor, coming together to save and mutually contribute to a common fund.
 
• They provide members with support and resources to improve their living standards and economic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance**:
 
 
• It is a financial service for low-income individuals or those who do not have access to typical banking services.
 
• Microfinance includes loans, savings, insurance, and fund transfers to help the underprivileged.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**:
 
 
• It is the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit for vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• Financial inclusion aims to connect people to the formal banking system to promote economic growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Livelihood Promotion**:
 
 
• It involves creating and enhancing opportunities for the poor to improve their income and employment prospects.
 
• Livelihood promotion includes training, skill development, and access to markets and financial services.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts of 1947 regulates the Indian labour law with regard to trade unions as well as individual workmen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Industrial Disputes Act**__**. ** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​The **Indian Labour Law** is governed by the **Industrial Disputes Act, 1947** in as much as it relates to** trade unions **and specific workers employed in any industry on the Indian mainland.
 
• The Act also establishes:
 
 
• a clause that provides for the** worker to be compensated** in the event of a **shutdown, layoff, or retrenchment.**
 
• the process for obtaining** advance approval **from the relevant government to** lay off employees, retrench them or shut down** industrial facilities.
 
• the steps to be taken in response to** unfair labour practices** by an **employer, a trade union, or employees**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act:**

 
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1861** was an Act of the British Parliament that changed the way** India's executive council operated** such that it operated as a cabinet with a** portfolio structure**.
 
• **Six "ordinary members" **made up this cabinet, each in charge of a different division of the **Calcutta government: the home, revenue, military, law, finance, and (from 1874) public works.**
 
 
 
• **Charter Act:**
 
 
• The East India Company's** monopoly over India **was broken by the **Charter legislation of 1813.**
 
• Yet, the business was able to maintain its monopoly in** commerce with China **and** trade in tea with India.**
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**
 
 
• **The Imperial Legislative Council,** British India's legislature, passed the** Rowlatt Acts in February 1919**.
 
• The acts permitted the **incarceration of suspects without a trial **and allowed for the trial of some political crimes without juries.
